mainTopic: The weaker bond of a יבמה to her יבם regarding vows, and the משנה on ratifying or nullifying a wife's future vows in advance.
overview: The amud opens with two proofs from a ברייתא that the argument about a יבם annulling his יבמה's vows is about a case where he did מאמר, as רבי אמי said. The גמרא then explains the ברייתא's phrase 'and like other matters, so are vows.' רבא says it means this: a man is not stoned for being with a יבמה the way he would be for a נערה המאורסה, so the יבם's power over her vows is also weaker. רב אשי shows that the wording of the משנה points to the same idea. Next, a new משנה teaches that a husband who ratifies his wife's future vows in advance has said nothing. If he nullifies them in advance, רבי אליעזר says it works because of a קל וחומר. The חכמים disagree, because the פסוק ties הפרה to הקמה. The גמרא then asks how רבי אליעזר's advance הפרה works: do the vows take effect for a moment and then get cancelled, or do they never take effect at all? It begins asking what practical difference this makes, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to support רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks if a ברייתא supports רבי אמי, and points to the phrase 'whether he did מאמר or not.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there a ברייתא that agrees with רבי אמי? Yes, since it teaches: 'Whether he performed מאמר with her or did not perform מאמר with her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for רבי אמי from the wording of a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said the argument is about a יבמה with whom the יבם did מאמר. The ברייתא says 'whether he did מאמר or not.' Saying 'even if he did מאמר' only makes sense if the case under debate is one where he did מאמר.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him
A יבם's betrothal of his יבמה done with money or a document, before full יבום
A widow waiting for יבום with her late husband's brother

phrases.english: Is it taught in agreement with רבי אמי?
Yes, since it teaches: whether he performed מאמר with her
or he did not perform מאמר with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אמי's statement from the earlier discussion that the dispute is about a case of מאמר.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's view that the dispute is about a יבמה with whom מאמר was done.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's phrase 'whether he performed מאמר or not.'

steps.title: A second proof from the first clause of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'she is fully his' only makes sense if he did מאמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, you can prove it from the first part, which teaches: 'Once she entered his domain, she is fully his.' If he did not do קידושין with her, what does 'fully his' mean? So learn from it that the case is where he did מאמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to prove רבי אמי right, this time from the opening words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says she is 'fully his.' Without any מאמר, the יבם has done nothing to make her his, so that phrase would be meaningless. It must be talking about a case where he did מאמר.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve the question from it; learn from it

phrases.english: Alternatively, from the first clause, which teaches:
Once she entered his domain, she is fully his.
And if he did not betroth her,
what does 'she is fully his' mean?
Learn from it that it is where he performed מאמר with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate proof for the same point as step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's view that the dispute is about a case of מאמר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first clause of the ברייתא: 'Once she entered his domain, she is fully his.'
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs show the same thing: the argument about a יבם annulling vows is about a יבמה with whom he already did מאמר.

steps.title: What does 'and like other matters, so are vows' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks to explain a hard phrase in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'and like other matters, so are vows,' which the ברייתא teaches?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what an unclear phrase in the ברייתא means. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase compares vows to 'other matters' but never says which matters or what the comparison shows. The גמרא wants to know what is being compared.

keyTerms.meaning: And like other matters, so are vows

phrases.english: What is 'and like other matters, so are vows,' which it teaches?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי וְכִשְׁאָר דְּבָרִים כֵּן נְדָרִים דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from proving רבי אמי right to explaining a phrase in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which 'other matters' are vows being compared to, and what does the comparison show?

steps.title: רבא: not stoned like a נערה המאורסה, so vows are the same
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the comparison: a יבמה is not treated like a betrothed girl for סקילה, and so too for vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, this is what it teaches: Don't you agree that one is not liable to סקילה for being with her, the way he would be for a נערה המאורסה? So too with vows.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the phrase: the 'other matter' is the punishment of סקילה, and vows follow the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who is with a נערה המאורסה is stoned, because her betrothal is a full bond. A man who is with a יבמה, even after מאמר, is not stoned. This shows her bond to the יבם is weaker, so according to this side of the ברייתא he also lacks a husband's power to annul her vows.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching
Stoning, a death penalty of בית דין

phrases.english: רבא said, this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין סְקִילָה,
phrases.english: Don't you agree that they are not liable to stoning,
phrases.notes: He means an outside man who is with a יבמה, who is tied to her יבם, even after the יבם did מאמר with her.

phrases.english: as with a betrothed young girl?

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'other matter' is סקילה: a יבמה's bond is weaker than a betrothed woman's, so vows are weaker too.
steps.confusionAlert: She is still a יבמה tied to him. The point is only that this bond is weaker than a full betrothal, so the husband-like rules like stoning and annulling vows do not apply to it.

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה's wording also shows this
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a יבמה is not 'fully' her husband's like a betrothed woman, which matches רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said, our משנה is also exact about this: 'A יבמה is not fully her husband's in the same way that a betrothed woman is fully her husband's.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for רבא's idea from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word 'fully' (גמורה). That word shows the משנה is comparing how complete each bond is. A יבמה's bond is less complete than a betrothal, which is exactly רבא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is also precise about this

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא:
phrases.english: רב אשי said: our משנה is also precise about this:
A יבמה is not fully her husband's
in the same way that a betrothed woman is fully her husband's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the משנה for רבא's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's explanation that a יבמה's bond is weaker than a betrothal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording: 'A יבמה is not fully her husband's like a betrothed woman.'
steps.whatToRemember: A יבמה, even after מאמר, is bound to the יבם less strongly than a betrothed woman is to her husband. That is why there is no סקילה, and why (according to this view) he cannot annul her vows.

steps.title: Ratifying vows in advance does nothing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a husband who ratifies, in advance, vows his wife has not yet made has said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who says to his wife, "All the vows you will make from now until I return from such-and-such place are hereby ratified," has not said anything.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a case where a husband tries to ratify (הקמה) his wife's future vows ahead of time. The ruling is that his words have no effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can normally ratify or nullify a vow after his wife makes it. Here he tries to ratify vows that do not exist yet, and the משנה says this does nothing. This sets up the next case: what happens if he tries to nullify in advance instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: the opening text being discussed
He has said nothing; his words have no legal effect

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who says to his wife:
"All the vows that you will vow
from now until I come back from such-and-such place
are hereby ratified"
has not said anything.
phrases.notes: In other words, those future vows are not ratified at all. He can still deal with them when she actually makes them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the יבמה discussion in steps 1-5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ratifying future vows in advance has no effect.

steps.title: Nullifying vows in advance: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: If the husband says the future vows are nullified, רבי אליעזר says the הפרה works and חכמים say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said "They are hereby nullified," רבי אליעזר says they are nullified, and the חכמים say they are not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the opposite case, where the husband nullifies (הפרה) her future vows in advance. Here there is a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ratification everyone agreed it does nothing, but nullification is different. רבי אליעזר holds that advance הפרה works, while חכמים treat it like advance הקמה and say it does nothing. The next two steps give each side's reason.

phrases.english: If he said "they are hereby nullified"
Rabbi Eliezer says: it is nullified
and the Sages say: it is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case of nullification after the ratification case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: advance הפרה works. חכמים: it does not.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's logical argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues with a קל וחומר: if a husband can nullify a vow that already took effect, surely he can nullify one that has not yet taken effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: If he can nullify vows that have already become a prohibition, should he not be able to nullify vows that have not yet become a prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר backs up his view with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow the wife already made is in force and forbids something, and the husband can still cancel it. A vow that does not exist yet is weaker, since nothing is forbidden. So it should be even easier to cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a stronger case to a weaker one
Have come into a state of prohibition, meaning the vow is already in force

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
If he can nullify vows
that have come into a state of prohibition
shall he not nullify vows
that have not come into a state of prohibition?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הֵפֵר נְדָרִים שֶׁבָּאוּ לִכְלַל אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבי אליעזר's position in step 7
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that advance הפרה works
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from nullifying an existing vow

steps.title: The Sages answer from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the קל וחומר. The פסוק links ratifying and nullifying, so only a vow that can be ratified can be nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The פסוק says, "Her husband may ratify it and her husband may nullify it." Whatever can be ratified can be nullified. Whatever cannot be ratified cannot be nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי אליעזר with a פסוק that ties הקמה and הפרה together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts ratifying and nullifying side by side, which teaches that they apply to the same vows. Step 6 showed a future vow cannot be ratified. So it cannot be nullified either, and the פסוק overrides the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Her husband may ratify it and her husband may nullify it (במדבר ל:יד)

steps.whatToRemember: For חכמים, הקמה and הפרה go together. A vow that cannot be ratified yet, because it does not exist, cannot be nullified yet either.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Behold, it says
"Her husband may ratify it, and her husband may nullify it."
That which has come into the category of ratifying
has come into the category of nullifying;
that which has not come into the category of ratifying
has not come into the category of nullifying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר as a whole
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק makes הפרה depend on the ability to do הקמה, and a future vow cannot be ratified.

steps.title: How does רבי אליעזר's advance nullification work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי אליעזר, do the vows take effect for a moment and then get cancelled, or do they never take effect at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked: According to רבי אליעזר, do the vows take effect and then get cancelled, or perhaps they do not take effect at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with an איבעיא about the mechanism of רבי אליעזר's view. When the husband nullifies in advance, does the vow briefly start and then disappear, or does it never begin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both options agree the wife ends up not bound. The question is whether the vow has a moment of existence before the earlier הפרה wipes it out. Or does the advance הפרה block it from ever starting?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them (the Sages); an open question
They take effect and are then cancelled
They do not take effect at all

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides of this question follow רבי אליעזר, so both agree the advance הפרה works in the end. The question is only how it works, not whether it works.

phrases.english: GEMARA
A question was asked of them:
According to Rabbi Eliezer,
do they take effect and then become cancelled,
or perhaps they do not take effect at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explores how רבי אליעזר's ruling from the משנה works
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to רבי אליעזר, an advance-nullified vow briefly takes effect or never takes effect.

steps.title: What practical difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the two possibilities would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what case is there a practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for a case where the two options from step 10 would lead to different results, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the wife is not bound either way, the question could seem purely theoretical. The גמרא wants to show there is a real case where the answer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference results from it?

phrases.english: For what case is there a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two options in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where 'take effect and are cancelled' and 'never take effect' would give different results.
